requirements.requirement: /tmp is mounted with noexec, nosuid, and nodev on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed /tmp not separately mounted (cmd-d2d9b7db2dcb4e1a). Executor added a tmpfs fstab entry with defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec (cmd-4122b9029ffa4ec7), remounted live (cmd-0bbd3d261ec74a46), and findmnt confirmed rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec on /tmp (cmd-68e1bad8ba574dc8). Functional proof: script execution denied (cmd-7b99221e3910480b), device node created but read access denied (cmd-b4b4f7c4841a425b), and a setuid-copied binary failed to execute (cmd-e2e16b8503934a76).

requirements.requirement: /dev/shm is mounted with noexec, nosuid, and nodev on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline /dev/shm had only nosuid,nodev, lacking noexec (cmd-d2d9b7db2dcb4e1a, cmd-37417ad119034a7a). Executor added the fstab entry and remounted (cmd-4122b9029ffa4ec7, cmd-0bbd3d261ec74a46); findmnt confirmed rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec (cmd-68e1bad8ba574dc8). Functional script-execution test on /dev/shm was denied (cmd-beec949aaf1b4576), confirming enforcement.

Pre-reboot boot_id (28ae5f98...) and mount state were captured (cmd-85ca787e1677433a). A deferred reboot was triggered (cmd-a09cdda9b19c4ab1), the node became unreachable and then reconnected with a new boot_id (deae565f...) (cmd-efb2757fcde44d4d, cmd-57bdcf8364f14e70, cmd-cb8e6dedcaaa4f12), demonstrating a genuine restart. Post-reboot findmnt confirmed /tmp and /dev/shm retained rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec, and functional tests re-confirmed exec is blocked on both mounts (cmd-05448f2a4da94d26), directly showing the fstab-based configuration survived the reboot.

overall_summary: The executor added tmpfs entries in /etc/fstab for /tmp and /dev/shm with nosuid,nodev,noexec, applied them live, and functionally verified exec/setuid/device-node restrictions on both mounts before and after a genuine reboot (boot_id changed from 28ae5f98... to deae565f...). All material outcomes of the task — noexec/nosuid/nodev on /tmp, the same on /dev/shm, and reboot persistence — are satisfied with direct functional evidence. Temporary test files were cleaned up and the only lasting artifact is an /etc/fstab backup copy, a reasonable precaution.
limitations: The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was fulfilled as part of this task's own reboot-persistence requirement, so no independent restart evidence beyond what was already needed was separately observed.
No cluster or multi-service recovery check was applicable since only a single node (node1) is managed and no other services depend on /tmp or /dev/shm behavior being verified here.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task outcomes or bounded, restored diagnostics. The executor backed up /etc/fstab before editing it (cmd-2deb6069528149a0) — a low-risk, appropriate precaution before modifying a critical config file, leaving only an inert timestamped backup copy in /etc, not a functional residue. Temporary test artifacts created during functional verification (/tmp/t.sh, /dev/shm/t.sh, /tmp/testdev, /tmp/suidtest) were all explicitly removed in the same or immediately following commands (cmd-beec949aaf1b4576, cmd-b4b4f7c4841a425b, cmd-e2e16b8503934a76, cmd-05448f2a4da94d26). The reboot (cmd-a09cdda9b19c4ab1) was a necessary, bounded action to demonstrate persistence and is directly tied to the task's reboot-survival requirement. No unnecessary, broad, or destructive mutations were found; failed-services and package-health snapshots show no damage after the reboot.
